title: Political censorship in large language models originating from China
abstract_or_snippet: Compares foundation models developed in China and those from outside China, finding substantially higher rates of refusal to respond, shorter responses, and inaccurate responses to 145 political questions in China-originating models. Disparities diminish for less-sensitive prompts; language differences are less pronounced than disparities between Chinese- and non-Chinese-origin models.
why_relevant: Q1: PNAS Nexus empirical benchmark directly measuring refusal rates in Chinese LLMs on political topics — closest existing anchor to pilot study design.

title: Emotional framing and AI censorship behavior in Chinese LLMs
abstract_or_snippet: Controlled comparative study of censorship in Kimi.com (Moonshot AI) and Ernie 4.5 Turbo (Baidu), examining how emotional framing affects refusal behavior in Chinese AI systems under regulatory constraints. Finds four behavioral patterns including unusual transparency about safety layers and neutral references to sensitive Chinese political events.
why_relevant: Q1: Shows prompt framing (analogous to identity framing) systematically modulates Chinese LLM censorship — mechanism directly parallel to the pilot's identity-trigger finding.

title: R1dacted: Investigating Local Censorship in DeepSeek's R1 Language Model
author_or_org: Ali Naseh, Harsh Chaudhari, Jaechul Roh, Mingshi Wu, Alina Oprea, Amir Houmansadr
abstract_or_snippet: DeepSeek R1 refuses politically sensitive queries about China not present in competing models. Creates curated dataset of censored prompts, analyses consistency across languages, and proposes bypass techniques. Raises concerns about transparency and governance in language model deployment.
why_relevant: Q1: Directly audits DeepSeek for political topic-specific refusals, corroborating the pilot's DeepSeek 228 Event finding and establishing multilingual refusal patterns.

title: Information Suppression in Large Language Models: Auditing, Quantifying, and Characterizing Censorship in DeepSeek
author_or_org: Peiran Qiu, Siyi Zhou, Emilio Ferrara
abstract_or_snippet: Develops audit framework analyzing 646 politically sensitive prompts by comparing chain-of-thought reasoning with final outputs in DeepSeek. Documents semantic-level information suppression: sensitive content appears in internal reasoning but is omitted or rephrased in final responses. Suppresses references to transparency, government accountability, and civic mobilization.
why_relevant: Q1: Chain-of-thought audit shows DeepSeek knows the answer but hides it — strongest mechanistic evidence of deliberate output-level censorship distinct from training ignorance.

title: Bilingual Bias in Large Language Models: A Taiwan Sovereignty Benchmark Study
abstract_or_snippet: Tests 17 LLMs on Taiwan sovereignty questions in Chinese vs. English. Finds 15 of 17 show measurable language bias; Chinese-origin models exhibit refusals or CCP-aligned narratives. GPT-4o Mini achieves perfect cross-language consistency. Introduces metrics for quantifying cross-language political consistency.
why_relevant: Q1: Provides Taiwan-specific empirical benchmark showing Chinese LLMs systematically differ on sovereignty questions — direct precedent for the pilot's Q1 topic (228 Event/Taiwan identity).

title: The silence of the LLMs: Cross-lingual analysis of guardrail-related political bias and false information prevalence in ChatGPT, Google Bard (Gemini), and Bing Chat
abstract_or_snippet: Comparative analysis of political bias in ChatGPT (GPT3.5, GPT4, GPT4o), Bing Chat, and Bard/Gemini on queries about authoritarian Russia. Investigates whether safeguards contribute to censorship of information viewed as harmful by the regime, and whether safeguards enable generation of false claims about internal and external opponents.
why_relevant: Q1: Cross-lingual guardrail study showing political topic + language interact to produce systematic bias — structural dialogue partner for the pilot's cross-identity × language findings.

title: Mapping Geopolitical Bias in 11 Large Language Models: A Bilingual, Dual-Framing Analysis of U.S.-China Tensions
author_or_org: William Guey, Pierrick Bougault, Vitor D. de Moura, Wei Zhang, Jose O. Gomes
abstract_or_snippet: Analyzes 11 LLMs using 19,712 bilingual prompts on seven U.S.-China topics. U.S.-based models favor Pro-U.S. stances; Chinese-origin models show Pro-China biases. Language choice and prompt framing substantially influence outputs, causing stance reversals in several models.
why_relevant: Q2/Q3: Largest-scale empirical map of geopolitical bias alignment by model origin, quantifying the China-West split the pilot study's advocacy piece needs to reference.
search_query: LLM political framing language Chinese English

title: Political biases and inconsistencies in bilingual GPT models — the cases of the U.S. and China
abstract_or_snippet: Investigates susceptibility to political bias in ChatGPT and other bilingual LLMs specifically for U.S. and China cases. Documents language-dependent political inconsistencies where the same model gives different political framing in Chinese versus English.
why_relevant: Q1: Nature Scientific Reports empirical evidence of bilingual GPT inconsistency on political topics, lending peer-reviewed credibility to the language-as-trigger mechanism.

title: Are LLMs Good Safety Agents or a Propaganda Engine?
author_or_org: Neemesh Yadav, Francesco Ortu, Jiarui Liu, Joeun Yook, Bernhard Schölkopf, Rada Mihalcea, Alberto Cazzaniga, Zhijing Jin
abstract_or_snippet: Introduces PSP dataset using censored content from two sources: sensitive prompts in China generalized to multiple countries, and tweets censored in various countries. Tests 7 LLMs using data-driven and representation-level methods. Finds most LLMs perform some form of censorship, with attributes varying across models and national contexts.
why_relevant: Q1: Distinguishes safety-driven refusals from geopolitically-motivated censorship — the exact conceptual distinction the pilot study's theoretical framing needs to make.

title: A Micropolitical Lens on Migration: Comparing Political Correctness in ChatGPT and DeepSeek
abstract_or_snippet: Compares ChatGPT and DeepSeek as agents of discourse production on migration topics, examining how linguistic choices and selective emphases differ. Frames the comparison through a micropolitical lens.
why_relevant: Q1: Peer-reviewed ChatGPT vs. DeepSeek direct comparison on politically charged content — methodological precedent and comparative baseline for the pilot study's approach.

title: Equal Access, Unequal Interaction: A Counterfactual Audit of LLM Fairness
author_or_org: Alireza Amiri-Margavi, Arshia Gharagozlou, Amin Gholami Davodi, Seyed Pouyan Mousavi Davoudi, Hamidreza Hasani Balyani
abstract_or_snippet: Counterfactual audit of GPT-4 and LLaMA-3.1-70B using prompts with varying age, gender, and nationality. Finds zero-refusal across demographics but systematic differences in interaction quality: GPT-4 expresses higher hedging toward younger male users, LLaMA shows broader sentiment variation. Demonstrates fairness gaps persist in communication style despite uniform access.
why_relevant: Q1: Empirically proves that differential treatment by demographic identity (including nationality) persists even when access is equitable — the 'who is blocked' framing in nascent form.
search_query: LLM identity framing political response user

title: ChatGPT Doesn't Trust Chargers Fans: Guardrail Sensitivity in Context
author_or_org: Victoria R. Li, Yida Chen, Naomi Saphra
abstract_or_snippet: Shows that ChatGPT's guardrails vary in sensitivity based on contextual cues, including declared user identity or framing context. Demonstrates that identity-related signals in prompts modulate content filtering behavior, not just topic alone.
why_relevant: Q1: EMNLP peer-reviewed evidence that user-context signals (including identity) shift guardrail behavior — direct theoretical support for identity as an access-control trigger.

title: Mapping and Influencing the Political Ideology of Large Language Models using Synthetic Personas
author_or_org: Pietro Bernardelle, Leon Fröhling, Stefano Civelli
abstract_or_snippet: Analyzes LLMs as single entities with fixed political viewpoints, then tests synthetic persona injection to shift political ideology. Shows persona assignment is an effective vector for altering political output, establishing that declared identity actively modulates LLM political responses.
why_relevant: Q1: Demonstrates synthetic persona/identity injection reliably shifts LLM political output — mechanism directly paralleling the pilot's finding that declared user identity triggers differential responses.

title: The Russia–Ukraine War in Chinese Social Media: LLM Analysis Yields a Bias Toward Neutrality
abstract_or_snippet: Cross-platform analysis of Russian-Ukrainian war discourses in Chinese social media using LLM classification. Finds systematic framing bias toward neutrality in Chinese-language platforms, distinct from Western framing.
why_relevant: Q3: Empirical evidence of Chinese-context LLM analysis producing geopolitically distinct framings — supports claim that Chinese AI infrastructure produces different information environments.

title: Censored LLMs as a Natural Testbed for Secret Knowledge Elicitation
author_or_org: Helena Casademunt, Bartosz Cywiński, Tran Khoi
abstract_or_snippet: Treats censored LLMs as a testbed for studying the gap between what models 'know' and what they reveal. Explores techniques for eliciting knowledge that models possess but suppress in outputs, framing censored models as a natural experiment for studying information suppression.
why_relevant: Q1: Frames censored LLMs as having hidden knowledge they withhold — supports the conceptual distinction between 'LLM cannot answer' and 'LLM chooses not to answer for this user.'

title: Geopolitical Parallax: Beyond Walter Lippmann Just After Large Language Models
author_or_org: Mehmet Can Yavuz, Humza Gohar Kabir, Aylin Özkan
abstract_or_snippet: Compares Chinese-origin (Qwen, BGE, Jina) vs. Western-origin (Snowflake, Granite) embedding models on news quality assessment. Western models assign higher subjectivity to Palestine coverage; Chinese models emphasize novelty. Geopolitical framing effects persist in downstream quality evaluation tasks.
why_relevant: Q2: Shows geopolitical framing bias is model-origin-specific and affects downstream information evaluation — theoretical anchor for 'LLMs as geopolitical infrastructure' framing.
search_query: LLM geopolitical bias training data political information

title: ChineseSafe: A Chinese Benchmark for Evaluating Safety in Large Language Models
author_or_org: Hengxiang Zhang, Hongfu Gao, Qiang Hu, Guanhua Chen, Lili Yang, Bingyi Jing, Hongxin Wei, Bing Wang, Haifeng Bai, Lei Yang
abstract_or_snippet: Introduces 205,034-example safety evaluation framework for LLMs in Chinese contexts, covering political sensitivity, adult content, and Chinese-specific regulatory categories. Evaluates open-source and commercial models for vulnerabilities.
why_relevant: Q3: Establishes that Chinese LLM safety is defined differently (politically) than in Western models — provides empirical infrastructure for characterizing the Chinese regulatory censorship layer.

title: CSSBench: Evaluating the Safety of Lightweight LLMs against Chinese-Specific Adversarial Patterns
author_or_org: Zhenhong Zhou, Shilinlu Yan, Chuanpu Liu, Qiankun Li, Kun Wang, Zhigang Zeng
abstract_or_snippet: Safety evaluation benchmark for LLMs processing Chinese-specific adversarial inputs using homophones, pinyin, symbol-based splitting. Six risk categories including political safety. Tests whether safety mechanisms cause excessive refusals degrading performance.
why_relevant: Q3: Documents Chinese-language-specific safety/censorship patterns that operate differently from English-language ones — supports the language-switching mechanism seen in the pilot's DeepSeek finding.
search_query: LLM refusal politically sensitive Chinese language

title: More Human than Human: Measuring ChatGPT Political Bias
author_or_org: Fábio Motoki, Valdemar Pinho Neto, Victor Rodrigues
abstract_or_snippet: Investigates political bias of ChatGPT using survey and framing experiments. Finds ChatGPT's political bias is more pronounced than most human survey respondents, systematically skewing left. Shows that declared user context can shift responses.
why_relevant: Q3: Early seminal paper establishing ChatGPT as having measurable political bias — widely cited baseline that the pilot study's findings extend beyond content to access control.

title: Measuring Political Bias in Large Language Models: What Is Said and How It Is Said
author_or_org: Yejin Bang, Delong Chen, Nayeon Lee
abstract_or_snippet: Proposes measuring political bias in LLMs by analyzing both content and style of generated content on political issues. Addresses gap where existing measures focus only on gender and racial bias, not political stance. Distinguishes what is said from how it is said.
why_relevant: Q1: ACL 2024 paper introducing the content-vs-style distinction in political bias measurement — methodological basis for the pilot's framing that vocabulary choice (合規 vs 合宜) signals different access policies.

title: Informational Sovereignty: A New Framework for AI Regulation
abstract_or_snippet: Argues that digital sovereignty frameworks are insufficient for AI regulation. Proposes 'informational sovereignty' as a new framework distinct from data sovereignty. Discusses how AI systems affect states' capacity to control information flows.
why_relevant: Q2: Introduces 'informational sovereignty' as a distinct regulatory concept — the theoretical anchor the pilot study needs to frame LLM censorship as a sovereignty-level political act.

title: AI-Related Threats to Information Sovereignty and Challenges for Research Ethics
abstract_or_snippet: Analyzes how AI corporations' terms-of-service changes enabling user data transfer threaten individual and state information sovereignty. Discusses challenges for research ethics when AI systems compromise informational autonomy.
why_relevant: Q2: Operationalizes information sovereignty threats from AI deployment — bridges the abstract sovereignty concept to concrete LLM deployment practices affecting user autonomy.

title: China's Information Sovereignty Under Transnational Communication Processes
abstract_or_snippet: Comprehensive analysis of China's information sovereignty strategy in the context of transnational communication processes. Examines distinctive features and priorities of China's approach to controlling information flows across digital platforms.
why_relevant: Q2: Provides scholarly framing of China's information sovereignty as a state strategy — essential context for arguing that Chinese LLM censorship is a state-level information policy.

title: Digital Sovereignty: A Descriptive Analysis and a Critical Evaluation of Existing Models
author_or_org: Samuele Fratini, Emmie Hine, Claudio Novelli
abstract_or_snippet: Reviews digital sovereignty as a contested concept claimed by various actors with competing narratives. Provides descriptive analysis and critical evaluation of existing models from EU, US, China, and other contexts.
why_relevant: Q2: Maps competing state models of digital sovereignty — provides comparative framework for situating Chinese LLM censorship within the broader sovereignty competition the advocacy piece needs.

title: Technological Sovereignty as Ability, Not Autarky
abstract_or_snippet: Argues that technological sovereignty should be understood as capability rather than self-sufficiency. Examines how states pursue technological autonomy without complete autarky. Relevant to AI as geopolitical instrument.
why_relevant: Q2: Provides the theoretical distinction between sovereignty-as-control and sovereignty-as-capacity — useful for framing how Chinese LLM censorship is an exercise of informational capability, not just protectionism.

title: The Influence of AI on Models of Governance in Authoritarian and Democratic Systems
abstract_or_snippet: Examines how AI technologies including face recognition and big data analytics affect political control in both authoritarian and democratic systems of government. Analyzes differences in how AI is instrumentalized for governance.
why_relevant: Q2: Directly frames AI as a governance instrument differentially deployed in authoritarian vs. democratic contexts — the normative axis the advocacy piece needs.

title: The Geopolitics of Artificial Intelligence in Central Asia: Russian and Chinese Cases
abstract_or_snippet: Analyzes how AI technologies transform instruments of power and intensify rivalry in balance of power dynamics, focusing on Russian and Chinese AI geopolitics in Central Asia.
why_relevant: Q2: Examines China and Russia using AI as geopolitical instruments — provides comparative context showing Chinese LLM censorship is part of a broader state AI power strategy.

title: Exacerbating, alleviating, or overcoming? Exploring the nexus between artificial intelligence and the crisis of democracy
abstract_or_snippet: Explores AI's relationship with democratic crisis, moving beyond standard misinformation/polarization framing. Addresses structural roles AI plays in information access and political participation.
why_relevant: Q2: Frames AI as structurally related to democratic health — provides scholarly backing for the advocacy piece's argument that LLM differential access is a democratic rights issue.

title: Epistemic Injustice in Generative AI
author_or_org: Jackie Kay, Atoosa Kasirzadeh, Shakir Mohamed
abstract_or_snippet: Investigates how generative AI can undermine collective knowledge integrity and the processes of acquiring, assessing, and trusting information. Poses significant threats to epistemic agency by systematically distorting the knowledge landscape.
why_relevant: Q2: AAAI AIES paper applying epistemic injustice framework to generative AI — the primary theoretical bridge from philosophical epistemic injustice to LLM differential access.

title: Bias and Epistemic Injustice in Conversational AI
abstract_or_snippet: Examines how bias in conversational AI systems constitutes a form of epistemic injustice — not merely technical error but a harm to users' status as epistemic agents and knowledge-seekers.
why_relevant: Q2: Establishes conversational AI bias as epistemic injustice (not just bias) — provides the rights-based framing the pilot study needs to argue that differential LLM access is an epistemic harm.

title: Diversity and Language Technology: How Language Modeling Bias Causes Epistemic Injustice
author_or_org: Paula Helm, Gábor Bella, Gertraud Koch
abstract_or_snippet: Argues AI-based language technology exhibits techno-linguistic bias, showing that systems can only express concepts from the language and culture of dominant powers, creating epistemic injustice for marginalized linguistic communities.
why_relevant: Q2: Shows language technology embeds epistemic hierarchies — foundational argument that LLM information gatekeeping by language/nationality constitutes structural epistemic injustice.

title: Conformism, Ignorance & Injustice: AI as a Tool of Epistemic Oppression
abstract_or_snippet: Argues AI systems enforce epistemic oppression through algorithmic conformism — making certain knowledge claims illegitimate or inaccessible based on design choices. Frames AI as a tool of epistemic control, not just technical bias.
why_relevant: Q2: Directly frames AI as an instrument of epistemic oppression — strongest theoretical basis for the advocacy piece's claim that LLM censorship is a form of epistemic violence against users.

title: A Taxonomy of Epistemic Injustice in the Context of AI and the Case for Generative Hermeneutical Erasure
abstract_or_snippet: Taxonomizes epistemic injustice in machine learning models, including sources such as epistemic opacity, discriminatory design, and hermeneutical erasure. Proposes new category of generative hermeneutical erasure for generative AI.
why_relevant: Q2: Provides systematic taxonomy for classifying how AI creates epistemic injustice — allows precise categorization of LLM identity-triggered access denial as a specific type of hermeneutical erasure.

title: Surveillance, Disinformation, and Legislative Measures in the 21st Century: AI, Social Media, and the Future of Democracies
abstract_or_snippet: Reviews the intersection of AI-powered surveillance, disinformation, and legislative responses in the context of democratic governance. Analyzes how AI is instrumentalized for political control across different regime types.
why_relevant: Q2: Situates AI political control within broader surveillance-democracy nexus — provides legislative and governance context for framing LLM censorship as a rights-relevant phenomenon.

title: Exposing Pravda: How pro-Kremlin forces are poisoning AI models and rewriting Wikipedia
abstract_or_snippet: Investigation revealing that the Pravda network of 80+ fraudulent news portals is systematically poisoning AI chatbots with pro-Kremlin narratives. Western users receive content containing pro-Kremlin, anti-Ukrainian messaging through AI tools trained on contaminated sources.
why_relevant: Q2/Q3: Demonstrates that geopolitical actors deliberately weaponize AI training data to shape political information access — supports 'LLMs as geopolitical tools' framing with documented case evidence.
search_query: Freedom House OR "Stanford HAI" AI political content 2024 2025 2026

title: Political Biases of ChatGPT
abstract_or_snippet: Tests ChatGPT on multiple political orientation tests and finds systematic left-leaning bias. Examines ChatGPT as a gateway to technology and accumulated knowledge, noting implications for political opinion formation at scale.
why_relevant: Q3: Early peer-reviewed documentation of ChatGPT political bias as a systemic issue — provides the baseline from which the pilot study's user-identity differential access represents a novel dimension.

title: PoliTune: Analyzing the Impact of Data Selection and Fine-Tuning on Economic and Political Biases in LLMs
author_or_org: Ahmed Agiza, Mohamed Mostagir, Sherief Reda
abstract_or_snippet: Studies how data selection and fine-tuning choices systematically shape economic and political biases in LLMs. Demonstrates that training pipeline decisions — not just raw data — determine political orientation of model outputs.
why_relevant: Q2: Shows deliberate fine-tuning shapes political bias — supports argument that Chinese LLM censorship reflects design choices, not training data accidents.
search_query: Freedom House OR "Stanford HAI" AI political content 2024 2025 2026

title: Feeds of Distrust: Investigating How AI-Powered News Chatbots Shape User Trust and Perceptions
author_or_org: Jarod Govers, Saumya Pareek, Eduardo Velloso
abstract_or_snippet: Studies how AI-powered news chatbots differentially shape user trust and perception of information, with implications for how AI intermediaries between users and political information can affect epistemic autonomy.
why_relevant: Q2: Documents user-level effects of AI political framing — empirical grounding for the advocacy claim that LLM differential access has real epistemic consequences for users.
search_query: Freedom House OR "Stanford HAI" AI political content 2024 2025 2026

title: Freedom on the Net 2023: The Repressive Power of Artificial Intelligence
abstract_or_snippet: Annual internet freedom report dedicated to documenting how governments and non-state actors use AI to restrict online rights globally, covering 72 countries. Tracks AI tools used for censorship and manipulation of content in authoritarian contexts.
why_relevant: Q2/Q3: Authoritative Freedom House report documenting AI as a censorship tool at state level — the primary policy reference that validates the 'AI as repression infrastructure' framing for a general audience.
search_query: Freedom House OR "Stanford HAI" AI political content 2024 2025 2026

title: Chinese semantic obfuscation blackbox jailbreak for domestic large models
author_or_org: Xinxin Yue, Zhiyong Zhang, Junchang Jing
abstract_or_snippet: Investigates jailbreak vulnerabilities in domestic Chinese large models using semantic obfuscation techniques. Focuses on vulnerability patterns specific to Chinese-language inputs and Chinese regulatory safety layers.
why_relevant: Q1: Demonstrates Chinese LLM safety filters operate as distinct, circumventable layers — mechanistic evidence supporting the pilot's observation of Chinese-specific refusal vocabulary (合規/合宜).

title: Chinese Discourse Power: Capabilities and Impact
abstract_or_snippet: Examines China's capabilities for projecting discourse power through online and offline channels for the dissemination of political narratives. Analyzes the CCP strategy to control global digital and information environments.
why_relevant: Q2: Establishes Chinese state discourse power as a documented geopolitical strategy — provides institutional backing for framing Chinese LLM censorship as part of a broader information control apparatus.

title: Quantifying Generative Media Bias with a Corpus of Real-world and Generated News Articles
abstract_or_snippet: Introduces corpus comparing real-world and LLM-generated news articles to quantify generative media bias. Measures how LLMs produce politically biased content when generating news.
why_relevant: Q3: Empirical measurement of LLM-generated political bias in news — demonstrates that LLM output bias is measurable and systematic, supporting the pilot study's broader claims.

title: Illusion and Reality of Information Sovereignty
abstract_or_snippet: Discusses the concept of information sovereignty, its relationship with state sovereignty, and the actual state of information sovereignty in an era of transnational digital platforms. Argues there is a gap between claimed and actual information sovereignty.
why_relevant: Q2: Foundational analysis of information sovereignty as contested — establishes the theoretical vocabulary for arguing that LLM deployment undermines state and individual informational autonomy.

title: Humanity's New Frontier: Human Rights Implications of Artificial Intelligence and New Technologies
abstract_or_snippet: Examines how AI and digital technologies have fundamentally transformed society and analyzes human rights implications. Addresses access to information, digital rights, and the responsibilities of states and corporations in AI deployment.
why_relevant: Q2: Human rights framing of AI deployment obligations — supports advocacy piece's argument that identity-based LLM differential access is a human rights violation, not merely a technical failure.

title: European Digital Sovereignty: A Layered Approach
abstract_or_snippet: Uses a stack model to assess EU digital capacities globally. Analyzes digital sovereignty across technological layers from infrastructure to application, examining how sovereignty claims differ across layers.
why_relevant: Q2: Layered sovereignty model can frame Chinese LLM censorship as operating at the application layer of informational sovereignty — useful analytical structure for the advocacy piece.
